subject.title: fix(line): dripping inbound media downloads hang past setup timeout

question: Should LINE inbound media intentionally fail closed after a fixed 120-second response-body lifetime, even when bytes are still progressing?
rationale: Source and loopback evidence establish the hang and the implementation mechanism, but repository precedent cannot determine the acceptable LINE-specific cutoff for unusually slow healthy attachments.

options.title: Approve 120 seconds
options.body: Keep the proposed fixed deadline, matching the cited Slack and Feishu total-transfer precedent while bounding all dripping bodies.

options.title: Choose a longer fixed limit
options.body: Retain the same implementation but select a LINE-owner-approved deadline that reduces false failures for slow large media.

options.title: Pause for live measurement
options.body: Hold the PR until representative live LINE video or audio transfers establish an appropriate production body budget.

recommendation.title: Approve 120 seconds
recommendation.body: Keep the proposed fixed deadline, matching the cited Slack and Feishu total-transfer precedent while bounding all dripping bodies.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the current LINE readiness and content-stream ownership path and are the strongest history-backed routing candidate for this contract choice.
